title: Super assets surge past $4.7tn as contributions climb
full_text:
Australia’s superannuation assets have climbed 9.5 per cent over the year to reach $4.77 trillion, as contributions into the system grew at a faster pace than benefit payments.
The Australian Prudential Regulation Authority’s (APRA) latest Quarterly Superannuation Performance report showed total industry assets increased from $4.35 trillion in June 2025 to $4.77 trillion at the end of June 2026.
Growth accelerated during the June quarter, with total superannuation assets rising 6.6 per cent over the three months to approximately $4.8 trillion.
APRA-regulated funds accounted for the majority of the system, holding $3.41 trillion in assets at the end of June, an increase of 11.9 per cent from $3.05 trillion a year earlier.
Self-managed super fund (SMSF) assets grew at a slower rate, increasing 3.6 per cent from $1.07 trillion to $1.11 trillion over the same period.
Assets held by exempt public sector superannuation schemes increased 5.6 per cent to $187.8 billion, while the balance of life office statutory fund assets edged 1.2 per cent higher to $60.7 billion.
The expansion in the system came alongside double-digit growth in contributions, which increased 12.8 per cent to $236.3 billion over the year to June 2026.
Employer contributions remained the largest source of inflows and rose 9.5 per cent over the year to $164.4 billion, while member contributions recorded considerably stronger growth.
Member contributions increased 21.0 per cent to $71.9 billion, representing an increase of about $12.5 billion compared with the previous year.
While money flowing into super accelerated, the amount being paid out to members also continued to rise, with total benefit payments increasing 12.1 per cent to $148.2 billion over the year.
Lump sum payments rose 13.0 per cent to $82.5 billion, while pension payments increased 11.0 per cent to $65.7 billion.
Despite the increase in withdrawals, contribution growth remained slightly ahead of benefit payment growth over the year.
Among entities with more than six members, net contribution flows increased 9.6 per cent from $70.9 billion in the year to June 2025 to $77.7 billion in the year to June 2026.
The latest figures leave the APRA-regulated sector responsible for more than $3.4 trillion of Australia’s overall $4.77 trillion superannuation system.
